Tim — thanks for the clear checklist. High level answers below and I attached the roster and a concise runbook summary for CardioHealth review.

- Subprocessor roster: see attached spreadsheet (subprocessor_roster_v3.xlsx). We included region, purpose, and whether they have persistent access to plaintext data. Only the analytics subprocessor in APAC has transient replicated telemetry access during controlled failovers.
- KMS/HSM: customer keys remain in your selected KMS by default. For failover we use an envelope-key approach: a region-specific wrapping key is used on-host and audit logs record wrap/unwrap operations. We do not persist unwrapped keys outside the pinned region — the transient path unlocks brief use via a dedicated HSM cluster with strict TTL.
- Egress runway (summary in egress_runbook_summary.pdf): triggers (regional outage, degraded latency > 250ms for 15 minutes), telemetry (metrics + per-request trace id, bitrate + token counts), notification windows (15m pre-failover notification when possible, otherwise immediate post-event notification), and rollback (automatic routing back after 30 minutes of healthy metrics + manual confirmation).

Next steps:
1) Legal: Marissa, can you prepare a DPA addendum that captures the transient replication window, audit requirements, and an approval flow for exceptions?
2) Tech: Karthik/Jonas, please confirm the HSM TTL and whether the analytics worker requires additional encryption-in-use controls.
3) Tim: once you confirm this draft roster/runbook is acceptable, we’ll route the addendum for signature.

I attached both files and a Drive link to the full runbook for your team. Happy to join a quick call — I have availability Monday afternoon.

—

Quick technical clarifications from our side:

- HSM TTL: we currently set transient unwrap TTL to 2 hours by default for failover paths; for CardioHealth we can reduce to 1 hour if you prefer, with additional operator approvals.
- Analytics worker in APAC: it processes aggregated telemetry only (no raw PII). We will add an AES-GCM encryption-at-rest + per-batch ephemeral wrapping key and log key access events to the customer audit stream.
- Canary strategy: on failover we route 1% of traffic through the APAC analytics path for the first 10 minutes; this is observable via tracing and we can auto-abort if error rate > 1.5%.

Action items I’ll take: upload the HSM config snippet to the Drive link Markus shared and add the canary-safety thresholds.
